newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia confirms delay to VAT launch.
newsitem.headline: Croatia confirms delay to VAT launch.

text.p: Croatia has indefinitely postponed the introduction of a 22 percent VAT (Value-Added-Tax) which had been due to take effect January 1, 1997, a senior government official said on Friday.
Parliament passed a bill in 1995 stipulating that a single 22 percent VAT would replace a complicated turnover tax from the beginning of 1997.
The senior official confirmed reports in pro-government media that the ruling party -- Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) -- decided earlier this week to put off the launch of a VAT.

Analysts said the HDZ, led by President Franjo Tudjman, feared that a sudden steep rise in prices could cause social unrest and damage its chances for re-election in presidential and communal voting due next year.

"The implementation of the Value Added Tax would surely lead to a rise in prices of some strategic products, including foodstuffs," a high-ranking HDZ source was quoted by the Zagreb newspaper Vjesnik as saying.
He said the VAT would be postponed for at least few months.
